question: Which Amendment to the Constitution of India removed the 'Right to property' from the Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is **__44th Constitutional Amendment 1978.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The Constitution 44 Amendment Act of 1978 made the right to property no longer a fundamental right. 
 
• Originally, one of the seven essential rights was the right to property, which stated that no one may be stripped of their property except by legal authority.
 
• After the 44th Amendment Act of 1978, the right to property as a Fundamental Right was replaced with a legal right under Article 300A of Part XII of the Constitution.
